subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage: I'm Deepak, and I became a shift supervisor at twenty-five. The first time Mahima, one of my juniors, left the packing area unlocked overnight, I nearly said something sharp in front of the team. I felt my voice rising, so I waited until the floor emptied. Then I said, "Last night the packing area was left unlocked from 9 to 6. That put the stock at risk, and I had to explain it to the manager. I'd like you to use the checklist at closing. What would help you remember?" She said the checklist was in the office, not at the door. We moved it. I hadn't used sarcasm or a lecture, and I checked in only once more after that. She hasn't slipped since.

qa.q: Where did Mahima say the checklist was kept?
qa.a: In the office, not at the door.

qa.q: What was Deepak feeling before he spoke to Mahima, and how did Deepak handle it?
qa.a: Deepak felt irritated and noticed the rising voice, so Deepak waited until the floor emptied and spoke calmly.

qa.q: What made Deepak's reprimand more effective than a sharp remark in front of the team?
qa.a: Deepak described the behaviour and its impact, stayed calm and asked what would help, so Mahima could fix the problem without humiliation.

qa.q: How might Mahima have felt if Deepak had scolded her in front of the team?
qa.a: She might have felt humiliated and defensive, and been less willing to say the checklist was in the wrong place.

grounding: A young supervisor reprimands by describing the behaviour and its impact, keeping calm and giving a path to improve.

subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage: Note from Uma, operations head. I observed Jaya, a new supervisor, speak to a trainee about repeated late arrivals. Jaya took the trainee aside, away from the others, and said in an even voice, "For three mornings you've come after the briefing started. The team has had to repeat the instructions for you, and it slows the start. I want you here by the briefing. Is something making it hard?" The trainee explained about the bus timetable. Jaya offered to move the trainee to the later group for two weeks and to review then. There was no sarcasm and no raised voice. Afterwards Jaya asked me if she had been too soft. I told her that clear and calm is not soft, and suggested she write the review date down.

qa.q: How many mornings had the trainee arrived after the briefing began?
qa.a: Three mornings.

qa.q: What was Jaya worried about when she asked Uma if she had been too soft?
qa.a: She worried that being calm and kind might not be firm enough; Uma's answer suggests her approach was fine.

qa.q: What could Jaya do to make sure the plan works?
qa.a: She can write down the review date and check in then, as Uma suggested.

qa.q: How might the trainee have felt being spoken to away from the others?
qa.a: They probably felt less embarrassed and more able to explain about the bus timetable.

grounding: A young supervisor reprimands calmly, describing the behaviour and its impact, listening to the cause and offering a path to improve, seen by a senior.

subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage:
Friday night
Had to talk to Mahima today about being late. Fourth time this month, and the breakfast rush fell apart again because the coffee station wasn't ready.
I remember how my old supervisor at the bakery used to do it: sarcasm in front of everyone. "Oh, look who decided to join us, the princess." I used to cry in the storeroom. I swore I'd never do that.
So I took Mahima to the back at the end of the shift, just us, and kept my voice low. "You've come in after eight four times this month. When the coffee station isn't set up, the whole line waits and customers walk out. I need you here by 7:45. Is something making mornings hard?" She went quiet, then said the bus route had changed. We worked out an earlier bus, and she'll message me by seven if she's stuck.
She thanked me. I didn't enjoy it, but I didn't feel like a bully either.
Noor

qa.q: By what time does Noor need Mahima to arrive?
How did Noor feel remembering the old supervisor?
qa.a: Noor remembered feeling humiliated and hurt, crying in the storeroom, and was determined never to treat anyone that way.

qa.q: How did Noor reprimand Mahima well?
qa.a: In private and with a calm voice, Noor described the behaviour and its impact, stated the expectation, asked what made mornings hard and agreed a plan.

qa.q: How did Mahima respond to the conversation?
qa.a: Mahima went quiet, explained the changed bus route, agreed a plan and thanked Noor, suggesting she felt respected rather than shamed.

grounding: Shows a young supervisor reprimanding privately by naming the behaviour and its impact and giving a path to improve, avoiding sarcasm and humiliation.

subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage:
Trisha: Sudha, do you have 10 minutes this afternoon? want to talk about the client report
Sudha: sure. is something wrong? 😟
Trisha: yes, and I'd rather talk than type it. 3pm, small meeting room?
Sudha: ok
(after the meeting)
Sudha: thanks for doing that privately. I was bracing for a public roasting like at my old job
Trisha: no roasting. the facts are just: the report went out with last month's figures, and the client noticed before we did. that hurt our credibility with them
Sudha: I know. I'm sorry. I'll use the checklist you showed me before every send
Trisha: good. and if you're overloaded, tell me BEFORE deadline day. that's the part I most want to change
Sudha: I will. honestly I was drowning that week
Trisha: then that's on both of us to catch earlier 👍

qa.q: What was wrong with the report that went out?
qa.a: It went out with last month's figures.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling before the meeting?
qa.a: Sudha felt worried and apprehensive, bracing for a public roasting like at Sudha's old job.

qa.q: How did Trisha handle the reprimand well?
qa.a: Trisha spoke privately, stated the facts and the impact on credibility, agreed a checklist, and asked Sudha to flag overload before deadlines.

qa.q: What would have changed if Trisha had criticised Sudha in front of the team?
qa.a: Sudha would likely have felt humiliated, as in the old job, and might have hidden being overloaded instead of admitting it.

grounding: Shows a young supervisor reprimanding privately and calmly, describing the impact and a path to improve rather than humiliating.

subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage: At the milk collection centre in the kasba outside Bathinda, Gurleen had been supervisor for six weeks. That morning three farmers complained that Imran had written the wrong fat readings in their passbooks again. The old foreman, Bhola-ji, muttered, "Shout at him in front of everyone. That's how he'll learn." Gurleen remembered being shouted at in her first job and how she'd learned nothing except fear. She waited till the tankers left and called Imran to the office. She kept her voice low. "Three farmers' readings were wrong today. When that happens, they think we're cheating them, and some may stop coming. I need every reading checked twice before you write it. What's making it hard?" Imran looked at the floor. "The machine display is faint. Sometimes I guess." Gurleen nodded. "Then we'll get the display fixed, and until then you read it aloud and Bhola-ji confirms." Imran's shoulders relaxed.

qa.q: How many farmers complained?
qa.a: Three farmers.

qa.q: What was Imran feeling when called to the office?
qa.a: Imran likely felt nervous and ashamed, looking at the floor as he admitted sometimes guessing the readings.

qa.q: How did Gurleen reprimand Imran effectively?
qa.a: She spoke privately and calmly, described the error and its impact on the farmers' trust, set a clear expectation, and fixed the real cause with a practical plan.

qa.q: How might the farmers see wrong readings?
qa.a: They might feel cheated and lose trust in the centre, and some might stop bringing their milk.

grounding: Shows a young supervisor choosing a calm, private reprimand that names impact and gives a path to improve instead of public shouting.

subtype: Scolding and reprimanding as a supervisor [Regulating]
passage:
At the Dublin distribution centre, Emeka watched Tomas drive the forklift out of the bay without doing the morning safety check, for the second time that week. The words that came to mind were sharp ones: "Nice of you to join us, rule-breaker." His own old supervisor used to talk like that, in front of everyone.
Instead he waited until the break and asked Tomas into the office.
"I saw you take the forklift out without the checklist today and on Tuesday," Emeka said, keeping his voice level. "If the brakes or the lifting chain fail, someone on the floor could be hurt, you included."
Tomas rubbed his neck. "The checklist takes ten minutes and the trucks are waiting."
"Then we fix that. You start ten minutes early next week, and I'll tell the drivers loading starts at 7:10. But the check happens every time."
Tomas nodded. "Okay. Every time."

qa.q: How long does the checklist take, according to Tomas?
qa.a: The checklist takes ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Emeka feeling when the sharp words came to mind?
qa.a: Emeka felt frustrated and worried about safety, tempted to use sarcasm like his old supervisor, but chose to stay calm.

qa.q: Which parts of Emeka's reprimand made it fair and useful?
qa.a: It was private, described the exact behaviour and its safety impact, stayed level, heard Tomas's reason and gave a clear path: start ten minutes early and check every time.

qa.q: How might Tomas have reacted to a sarcastic remark in front of everyone?
qa.a: Tomas would likely have felt humiliated and defensive, and might never have shared the real reason, the waiting trucks.

grounding: A young supervisor reprimands by describing the behaviour and its impact calmly and giving a path to improve, avoiding sarcasm and public humiliation.
